To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HLA-B-restricted epitopes show lower binding affinity and a more restricted binding pattern than HLA-A-restrictive epitopes.

1. the HLA-B peptide repertoire is less diverse than the HLA-A repertoire and the average peptide affinity of HLA-B is lower than that of the HLA-A peptides; 2. the diversity of peptide repertoire and peptide binding affinity are not the only parameters determining immunodominance.

HLA-B alleles are characterized by a less diverse and less tightly bound peptide repertoire than HLA-A alleles, which may explain why CD8+ T cells restricted by HLA-A molecules tend to be less immunodominant than those restricted by HLA- B molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the mechanisms that determine the immunodominance hierarchy of CD8+ responses and may contribute to the development of novel strategies to improve vaccine efficacy.
the identification of factors influencing the generation of CD8+ responses and their impact on the outcome of infectious diseases.
the question of whether differences in the diversity and peptide binding affinity of HLA-B versus HLA-A molecules may be responsible for the differences in CD8+ T lymphocyte responses.

HLA-B alleles are characterized by a less diverse peptide binding motif, which is in line with the observation that HLA-B-restricted responses are more dominant than HLA-A-restriced responses.
the HLA-B-restricted peptide repertoire is less diverse, but that the average affinity is lower, which may be a contributing factor for the immunodominance observed in HLA-B-represented responses.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HLA-B alleles are less permissive to binding a wide variety of peptide ligands and that the average binding affinity for HLA-B-restricted peptides is lower than for HLA-A-restrictive ligands, which may be the reason for the immunodominance observed for CD8+ T cells restricted by HLA class I molecules.
, in the case of HLA-B-restricted responses, a higher binding affinity of a peptide to its restricting HLA-B allele is not sufficient for a response to be dominant.

HLA-B-restricted responses are more restricted in terms of the number of epitopes, but that they are characterized by a higher affinity for the epitope-MHC class I complex, which might be a contributing factor to the dominance of these responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the peptide repertoire of HLA-B alleles is less diverse, and the respective epitopes have lower average binding affinity, than the peptide repertoire and epitopes restricted by HLA-A alleles.
the diversity of the peptide repertoire is not necessarily a good predictor of the strength of CD8+ responses.
the HLA-B locus, which is known to have the greatest number of alleles, has the least number of epitopes and the weakest average peptide binding affinity.
